eras.name: The First Ages

paragraphs.text: The Argivian Reckoning (AR) counts Dominaria's years from the birth of Urza, and the plane's elder dragons date from some twenty thousand years before it.
Only seven of them outlived the Elder Dragon War, which lasted for generations of humans while Nicol Bolas set the dragon clans on each other.
Five god-like Primeval Dragons once ruled Dominaria; when they fell, Averru of the Numena shut one of them, Rhammidarigaaz, under a Shivan caldera.
A Shivan dragon is often in no hurry to kill.
The Thran, humans who had come out of the east, ruled in their last age from Halcyon, capital of an empire of eight city-states.
In Shiv the Thran built the Mana Rig, a prototype factory for powerstones with sections made for goblin workers; a second Rig stood at Halcyon.
The empire fell around -5000 AR, in a war with Yawgmoth, a eugenicist it had exiled and then recalled to cure a disease.
Yawgmoth had taken control of an artificial plane and named it Phyrexia, and he joined it by a portal to the caves beneath the capital.
Rebbec, the architect of Halcyon, closed the way between the planes as the city died, and Yawgmoth stayed on the far side.

eras.years: From about 20,000 to about 5,000 years before the birth of Urza

eras.name: The Brothers' War

paragraphs.text: Urza and Mishra, brothers of Argive born at the two ends of one year, went to war in the end over two halves of one Thran powerstone.
Later historians counted years from that birth; the count is the Argivian Reckoning, written AR.
As students at Tocasia's dig the brothers learned artifice from Thran ruins and found the Caves of Koilos, where a sealed gateway led to Phyrexia.

At Koilos, among the last remains of Halcyon, each brother took half of a powerstone, the Mightstone and the Weakstone; about ten years later Mishra stepped through the portal that the stone had sealed and came back with dragon engines.
Urza became chief artificer of Yotia, and Mishra rose among the Fallaji once he could command a dragon engine that came out of the sands.
The war that followed is also called the War of the Artificers: it began in sneak attacks and double-dealing, lasted decades, and the machines on each side grew more intricate as it went.
Priests of the Brotherhood of Gix, who worshipped machines, worked their way into both camps and onto Mishra's council; by the last battle Mishra was becoming a machine himself.
Urza ended the war by setting off the Golgothian Sylex; the blast left almost nothing of Argoth and nothing of either brother's body.
Urza came back from death as a planeswalker, through the joining of the two stones, and the glaciers that the blast set moving went on to take Penregon.

eras.years: From the brothers' birth, year 0 of the Argivian Reckoning, to the Sylex Blast

eras.name: The Dark

paragraphs.text: The Dark is the name for the almost four centuries between the Sylex Blast and the full onset of the Ice Age.
As summers shortened and fertile country went to waste, fear put zealots in power.
Of Terisiare's nations only Almaaz survived the war: Argive broke up into the Northern Provinces, and its capital, Penregon, fell in 80 AR.
The Church of Tal grew from two Yotian sun cults into the government of many cities, and its Book of Tal ordered that no magician be left alive.
The Conclave of Mages was a citadel raised in the north on the ruins of the Monastery of Gix; it and its rival, the City of Shadows in Lat-Nam, sheltered mages from the Church.
Lord Ith led the Conclave; Mairsil the Pretender caged him for twelve years, and when Jodah and Sima freed him he killed Mairsil and destroyed the school.
Tivadar of Thorn, a soldier of Ghed at thirteen, thought the city-states were fighting the wrong enemy and later led the Knights of Thorn against the goblins.

eras.years: From the Sylex Blast to about 450 AR

eras.name: The Fall of the Sarpadian Empires

paragraphs.text: Icatia was Sarpadia's human empire: a prime minister governed it from Windenby for the king, its army stood on the phalanx, and its clerics of Leitbur stood against the Order of the Ebon Hand.
Sarpadia's five cultures fell around 170 AR, after the cooling that Urza's Sylex brought had set old allies fighting over wood, iron and food.
Orcs and goblins, driven from their caves by the winters, joined into one horde and overran the dwarves and then Icatia.
The elves of Havenwood had raised thallids as food; the thallids became aware and overran their keepers.
The thrulls rebelled against their masters in the Order of the Ebon Hand, destroyed the order and spread over the whole continent.
The Vodalia of today lies off Aerona; the older merfolk country of that name lay in the seas round Sarpadia until homarid raiders destroyed it, and its empress Galina later built the new empire.

eras.name: The Ice Age

paragraphs.text: The cold that began with the Sylex Blast held Dominaria for almost twenty-five centuries, and the planeswalkers Leshrac and Tevesh Szat used magic to make it last.
Clans fleeing the ice of Storgard set up Kjeldor around 2434 AR in eastern Terisiare; three city-states held most of its power, and its hot springs helped it through the cold.

King Darien won control of a splintered Kjeldor when a coup by the Knights of Stromgald and their ally, the necromancer Lim-Dûl, failed; the Balduvian barbarians became his allies, and in the Thaw the two lands merged as New Argive.
In 2934 AR the planeswalker Freyalise cast the World Spell, which ended the Ice Age and began the Thaw.
The spell rode the energy of a rogue plane's arrival; Freyalise worked it through the Ice Cauldron, her own copy of the Golgothian Sylex, and the safe havens that spread its force did not survive.
Heidar, master of the Cult of Rimewind, set out to reverse the Thaw with Phyrexian war-beasts he had found frozen in the Ronom Glacier; their magic drove him mad.

eras.years: From 450 AR to the World Spell of 2934 AR

eras.name: Urza's Academy

paragraphs.text: Urza and the mage Barrin opened their academy on Tolaria in 3285 AR, a war school for the Phyrexian invasion that Urza expected.
Urza would teach none but children, his precaution against Phyrexian sleeper agents; even so, one such agent killed Jhoira there in 3307 AR.
Karn, whom Jhoira had named and taught, went back in time for her; later, even with his memory capped at twenty years, he told himself every night that she was his friend.
Urza's time machine failed in that journey and left Tolaria in pockets of fast and slow time; Jhoira was stranded there for a decade, and Teferi hung burning in a bubble of slowed time.
On his card Karn is a silver golem, a legendary artifact creature.
The rebuilt school later fought off K'rrik's negators with the help of Jhoira, Teferi and their allies from Shiv.
For over eight hundred years Urza also ran the Bloodline Project, which bred mortal heroes to carry the Legacy against Yawgmoth.
Barrin fought for Benalia, Keld and Urborg in the Phyrexian Invasion, then brought his dead daughter Hanna home and cast Obliterate, which left nothing of Tolaria and killed him too.

eras.years: From the academy's founding in 3285 AR to its end in the Phyrexian Invasion

eras.name: Legends of Jamuraa and Madara

paragraphs.text: Between 3334 and 3336 AR the tyrant Johan of Tirras made war on the city-state of Bryce, which Hazezon Tamar governed.
Hazezon defended Bryce with warriors made of sand and with a tiger-man, Jaeger Ojanen, and later drew in Adira Strongheart and her Robaran Mercenaries.
A sandworm killed Jaeger; his son Jedit went after Johan, and in the last battle, at Efrava, a sand wurm swallowed Johan in his turn.
West of Jamuraa lie the islands of Madara, where three lines of mana cross, red, black and blue; that is why the elder dragon Nicol Bolas wanted them.
Bolas became Madara's god-emperor in 3455 AR, ruling an empire that a warrior queen had founded in about 3226 AR.
Three officers governed for him until one of them, the assassin Ramses Overdark, became his single regent.
Tetsuo Umezawa, once the emperor's champion, killed Overdark in single combat at the Imperial Shrine and then brought down the shrine itself, and with it Bolas's hold on Dominaria.

eras.years: Johan's War of 3334 to 3336 AR, and Bolas's rule in Madara from 3455 AR for about 150 years

eras.name: The Five Peoples of Caliman

paragraphs.text: Caliman lies south-east of Jamuraa; Tojira and her nightstalkers hold its swamp island of Dakmor, the elves of Norwood its northern forest, and the kingdom of Alaborn its southern plains.
Alaborn's soldiers carry firearms, which had not been seen on Dominaria before.
Tojira, the swamp queen, armed the nightstalkers that attack Alaborn: long-limbed, sharp-toothed beings of black mana, mounted on mechanical beasts.

eras.years: Undated; the cards alone tell this story

eras.name: The Wars of Jamuraa

paragraphs.text: The vanishing of Teferi's island out of time sent a ripple that three mages felt, and the three made Jamuraa their home to keep watch on it: Mangara, Jolrael and Kaervek.
The wizard Mangara, who came from Corondor, made peace among Femeref, Zhalfir and the Suq'Ata, and within a century the region flourished.
Kaervek, who wanted a nation of his own, turned Jolrael against Mangara, stirred the border quarrels afresh and lured the peacemaker to a meeting that ended with him shut inside an Amber Prison.
Kaervek's war on Zhalfir, Femeref and the Suq'Ata ran for more than a year, from 4195 to 4196 AR, while Teferi's isle reappeared after almost two centuries away.
Asmira gave her life to break the prison, and the freed Mangara sealed Kaervek inside an Amber Prison in his turn.
In 4205 AR Keldon raiders struck Jamuraa's northern coast, persuaded that it had once been Keldon land.
The city-states of the Kipamu League, reorganised by the wizard Barrin at Teferi's request, slowly gained ground.
The Keldon leader Latulla was exiled from Keld for trying to wake its Witch-Kings, and she died in the last battle on Jamuraa.
The League won, but Barrin lost his wife Rayne in that battle, and both he and Teferi lost faith in Urza's plans.

eras.years: From the Mirage War of 4195 AR to the Keldon invasion of 4205 AR

eras.name: The Weatherlight and the Invasion

paragraphs.text: The Weatherlight, a skyship whose engine could take it between planes, came to Sisay from her family, Zhalfirins who had kept it for Urza, its designer.

Sisay learned her trade as a pirate ship's cabin boy, scouted for Zhalfir's armies from the Weatherlight in the Mirage War, and hunted pieces of the Legacy, which she knew could kill the Lord of the Wastes.
Gerrard Capashen, whom Urza's Bloodline Project had bred to be the Legacy's heir, had left her crew; he came back when Sisay was abducted to Rath, where his adoptive brother Vuel ruled as Volrath.
The invasion began in 4205 AR with strikes on Benalia, and Urborg was soon taken as Phyrexia's staging ground.

The second stage was Rath, an artificial plane that its evincars had swollen with flowstone until it merged into Dominaria; the merger set the Stronghold and its armies down in Urborg and ended Rath as a plane.
Hanna, the navigator Gerrard loved, died of plague at Koilos; Yawgmoth's promise to raise her won Gerrard over, and in the duel that Yawgmoth then staged Gerrard beheaded Urza.
The Legacy was Urza's store of artifacts against Phyrexia, the silver golem Karn among them, and in the end the Legacy killed Yawgmoth.
Urza's spark passed to Karn, who became a planeswalker; neither Urza nor Gerrard survived.
Urborg keeps the war's marks: the ruins of the Stronghold, which magma covered inside its volcano, and the Heroes' Memorial that Freyalise raised to the dead.

eras.years: The voyage of the Weatherlight and the Phyrexian Invasion of 4205 AR

eras.name: The Mirari

paragraphs.text: Otaria recovered early from the Phyrexian Invasion, and newcomers such as elves and minotaurs joined peoples found nowhere else, the nantuko, cephalids and aven.
The Cabal, founded in 4050 AR by Virot Maglan, its Patriarch, worshipped profit and grew rich on pit fights and the betting on them.
The Mirari, made by Karn as no more than a probe, turned its holder's desires into fact, and those who saw it craved it.
Three holders in turn loosed a spell they could not stop and died of it: Kirtar of the Order, the emperor Aboshan, whose wave drowned the continent's north, and Chainer.
Kamahl fixed the Mirari to his sword and, under its sway, ran his own sister Jeska through; to be rid of it he went to the Krosan forest.
Laquatus, a merfolk ambassador and an old rival, followed Kamahl to Krosa to take the Mirari, and Kamahl killed him there with the sword.
Kamahl left the sword where Laquatus lay and took up the druids' life that the nantuko Thriss had shown him.

eras.years: About a century after the Phyrexian Invasion

eras.name: The Coming of Karona

paragraphs.text: Gorgon Mount, an overgrown hill, rose where Kamahl's sword stood in Krosa; around it the forest's beasts turned huge and mad, and the forest itself advanced even as rot hollowed its trees.
Nivea, whom Ixidor loved, was the first person killed by Phage the Untouchable, the cursed avatar that Jeska had become and whose touch rotted whatever it met.
Ixidor made the angel Akroma, a living illusion in the likeness of his dead wife Nivea, to avenge her; the angel lost her legs in the Grand Coliseum, and he gave her a jaguar's in their place.
Karona was all of Dominaria's mana in one body, made when Kamahl's Soul Reaper killed Akroma, Zagorka and Phage in the same moment.
Karona's power fed on faith, and almost every living thing hailed her as a goddess; what she lacked was a purpose, and she searched through five portals for an equal.
Her card names her Karona, False God, a legendary Avatar.

Karona raised her worshippers into an army and destroyed whole cities; at Sanctum she killed the three reborn Numena, until two creatures she trusted put the Mirari sword through her and left only Jeska alive, a planeswalker.

eras.years: Around 4306 AR, after the Mirari came to Krosa

eras.name: The Time Rifts and the Mending

paragraphs.text: Eight great rifts had torn the fabric of Dominaria by the time Karona died, and each new one widened the rest; together they starved the plane of mana and let its past leak into its present.
The Gathans were Keldons whom Gatha, a renegade pupil of Urza, had remade as monstrous warriors; Keld destroyed them in its Gathan Wars, and the time rifts let hordes of them back out of its past.
Radha, a Skyshroud elf and the Keldon warlord Astor's granddaughter, drove the Gathans out and rose to be Grand Warlord of a Keld of elves and humans together that no longer took slaves.
Each rift had its price: Teferi's spark for Shiv, Freyalise's life and nearly the whole forest for Skyshroud, and for Tolaria a journey by Karn back to the moment before Barrin's spell.

Jeska returned to Dominaria in search of Karn and closed rifts her own way, at Zhalfir, at Yavimaya and last over Otaria, where the rift was Karona's legacy; that one took her life and began the Great Mending.
From then on planeswalkers were mortal and far weaker than before.

eras.years: The years before the Mending of about 4500 AR

eras.name: The Age of Renewal

paragraphs.text: Seven Great Houses govern Benalia, with Capashen the strongest; their compact for sharing power dates from the years after the Mending, when New Benalia was built and the Church of Serra became the state's faith.
Generations of peace followed on a plane that the war of Urza and Mishra had once frozen; the new danger was the Cabal, a cult under the Demonlord Belzenlok.
The Cabal of Otaria, written off as dead by about 4500 AR, came to rule from the Stronghold in Urborg and worked its way into Shiv, New Argive, Benalia and the Suq'Ata lands.
Cabalists trying to call back their old god Kuberr opened the Abyss, and the demon Belzenlok who came through crippled them and turned the Cabal into his own death cult.
Belzenlok took other beings' names for himself: Lord of the Wastes from Yawgmoth, Doom of Fools from Tevesh Szat, and the forging of the Blackblade from Dakkon.
Jhoira found the Weatherlight's metal skeleton on the seabed off Urborg, restored its hull from a seed and manned the ship for war on the Cabal.

The Blackblade is a soul-drinking sword that the Cabal said Belzenlok had forged; Gideon Jura robbed the Cabal's vaults of it and wounded the demon with it, and at Liliana's hand the sword drank his soul.

eras.years: About 4560 AR, sixty years after the Mending

paragraphs.text: Sheoldred, the praetor of New Phyrexia's black faction, arrived in the Caves of Koilos, planted sleeper agents in every society of Dominaria, and in 4562 AR led an army against the plane.
The Mana Rig that the Phyrexians attacked from the caves of Cometia Crater was one Jhoira had repaired, after she made peace between the Ghitu and the goblins who were fighting over its remains.
Jhoira destroyed the Rig herself rather than let it be captured; Jaya Ballard died there, and Karn was taken to New Phyrexia.
Dominaria threw Phyrexia back twice, the second time after hundreds of battles that left its cities in ruins, and the war then widened to countless other planes.
Sheoldred carried the captive Karn home to New Phyrexia and there fell to Elesh Norn; Ajani, the planeswalker she herself had converted, cut off her head.

sentence.text: Benalia is the great human nation of western Aerona, a country of grain fields and limestone cities.
Shiv is a land of active volcanoes, home to dragons, goblins, the viashino and the Ghitu.
The elves of Llanowar keep to themselves in a vast old forest in the south of Aerona.
Yavimaya is an island forest of trees as large as cities, in the Terisian Isles.
Terisiare was a northern continent that has since broken into the Terisian Isles.
Sarpadia is a remote southern continent where five cultures fell and the thrulls took the whole land.
Tolaria was the island of Urza's academy, until Barrin's spell destroyed it.
Caliman is a large island in the far south, where magic and machines are used side by side.
Jamuraa is the largest continent on the plane, a land of deserts, forests and city-states.
Urborg is a marsh-covered tropical island in the Burning Isles, long fought over by witches and necromancers.
Otaria is a narrow continent east of Jamuraa, once shared by nomads, barbarians, druids and the Cabal.
The Keldons, tall grey-skinned warriors hardened to the cold, live in Icehaven, a subcontinent of Aerona.
